title: Tesla Optimus robot is now doing real factory work

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: What does the Tesla Optimus robot doing real factory work mean for the future of human labor and automation?

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Optimus now performs repetitive tasks like welding and lifting — powered by Tesla’s Dojo supercomputer and advanced actuation systems.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: If robots take over dangerous or monotonous jobs, what happens to workers? Will this lead to widespread unemployment or a new kind of economic divide?

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Engineers are designing human-robot collaboration zones, where workers oversee and guide robots — preserving skilled labor roles.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: Imagine a future where humans focus on creative and strategic work, while robots handle the physical and repetitive tasks — a more balanced society.

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: The future isn’t just about machines — it’s about how we shape their role in our shared progress.

video_cue: A Tesla factory floor with Optimus robots working alongside human engineers on an assembly line.
